newsitem.title: UK: US stocks mixed in London, Morris slips.
newsitem.headline: US stocks mixed in London, Morris slips.

text.p: Most U.S. stocks were little changed in London on Thursday as European investors took to the sidelines after another record rally on Wall Street, dealers said.
Activity was further dampened ahead of a holiday in Switzerland on Friday, they said.
Trading in Philip Morris Cos Inc shares enlivened an otherwise slow market, falling $7/16 to $45-1/2.
The decline was sparked by a ruling from a Florida judge who said on Wednesday tobacco companies cannot use public knowledge of the dangers of smoking as a defence.
The ruling strips cigarette makers of a key defence just before the start of Florida's billion-dollar Medicaid lawsuit trial.
"The only real volume we're seeing is in Morris," said one London dealer.
Shares in J.P. Morgan and Co Inc firmed $1/4 to $116-1/4 after news the group would acquire a 45 percent stake in American Century, dealers said.
Most other shares were trading close to their New York closing levels and dealers were expecting Wall Street to open mixed.
Elsewhere, September S&P 500 index futures were down 0.50 point to 956.65 on Globex at 1048 GMT, while September long bond futures slipped 2/32 to 116-10/32.

At 1230 GMT, weekly jobless claims will be published, along with the second quarter price index and price deflator. The Chicago Purchasing Managers report for July and the June help wanted index were due for release at 1400 GMT.
Key employment figures for June will be reported on Friday.
